contract.description: Write a durable memory for future sessions and get back the stored record: its id, resolved tome, scope, kind, tags and supersede outcome. Use it when the human states a preference, decision or correction ("always X", "never Y", "we switched to Z"), when work reveals a non-obvious constraint or gotcha, and when the human says something worth keeping verbatim - record it as they said it, not as your summary. Pick kind: journal for subjective progress notes; fact for statements that must still read true next week (decisions, rules, preferences). Pick scope: session for things that die with this session; project (requires projectId) for one codebase; global for cross-project truths about the human and their tooling; personal only for identity-level traits - the persona itself is human-curated, never write it here. A near-duplicate write in the same scope and kind supersedes the older record and the response names the replaced id; retrying the identical write is safe - it replays the original record (idempotentReplay=true) instead of storing a copy. Writes are tome-bound: the memory lands in your resolved tome, or in the tome you pass. upstream_unavailable means the embedding provider or store is unreachable - nothing was written, retry when it is back. maintenancePending=true on an otherwise successful call means the memory committed but duplicate supersede did not finish; replaying the same write converges it. Never store secrets or tokens.
contract.name: memory_remember
contract.title: Remember a memory
